proposals.hypothesis: Li3PO4 is a wide-gap, electronically insulating, Li-rich phosphate that is chemically compatible with both sulfide electrolyte and LiCoO2 and is a well-known protective coating. It is a strong baseline for the interface.
LiNbO3 is the classic LiCoO2 coating. Nb5+ is hard to reduce, the gap is large, and the Li-ion conductivity should limit interfacial resistance, so it is a reference for the oxide-coating family.
Li2ZrO3 is a wide-gap, Zr4+ oxide with high oxidative stability at 4 V and little tendency to react with sulfides, so it should act as an insulating barrier layer.
LiAlO2 is a wide-gap, Al3+ oxide that is electrochemically inert at 4 V and is a common Li-ion coating. It tests the Al-oxide family.
LiF has a very large band gap and is highly oxidation-resistant, so it should be insulating and stable at the cathode. Its low Li-ion conductivity is a possible drawback.
Li2SiO3 is a lithium-rich silicate with a wide gap and good oxidative stability. It provides a different silicate chemistry for comparison with the phosphates and borates.
Li3BO3 is a lithium-rich borate with a wide gap and low-density B-O framework, likely stable against sulfide and oxide cathode at 4 V. It tests the borate family.
LiTaO3 combines a wide gap with Ta5+, which is highly resistant to reduction, so it should be a stable insulating coating with reasonable Li conductivity.
Li5AlO4 is a very Li-rich aluminate with a wide gap. It is likely to be stable against the sulfide electrolyte and is a test of a high-Li-content oxide.
Li3Al(BO3)2 is a mixed borate with a wide gap and a stable framework. It may combine borate and aluminate stability and is a candidate for lower penalty at the interface.
